text: “What makes you stand out from everybody else who’s got something out there?”
author: Terrie Williams

text: “Become a letter writer. Send thank you notes and letters to everyone you interview with.”
author: Leslie Comar

text: “When you’re entering a business where there are so many people competing for the same roles, my best advice is: be prepared.”
author: Kellie Williams Jackson

text: “I believe in raw talent, where people just show up in Hollywood and land roles. But, I think there’s enough people like that. I think people should be trained and prepared.”
author: Kellie Williams Jackson

text: “…it’s important that you can tell the story in a brief synopsis. What’s the one-sentence log line? This story is about…You have to fill in the blanks and describe the beginning, middle and end.”
author: Winifred White Neisser

text: “There is no logical ladder. You have to figure out your own ladder.”
author: Nan Tepper

text: “The best piece of advice I got is from a lady named Virginia Watson. Virginia said, “Vivica, you ain’t the only cute girl out in Hollywood.’ I don’t think she knew how much I heard her, but I did.”
author: Vivica A. Fox

text: “You have to be more than a pretty face out here. Beauty’s a dime a dozen. What makes you different? What makes you special?”
author: Vivica A. Fox

text: “Someone can come into this program who has written a really solid script and has the personality we’re looking for. We will put them into the program based on that.”
author: Jack Gilbert

text: “Be realistic about your budget. This means even if you’re getting everything for free. Write down what it’s actually going to cost so that you know what your real costs are and you’re not surprised when you have to start paying for it.”
author: Norlynne Coar

text: “Be easy to get along with. People help people they like, and they prefer to work with people they like.”
author: Norlynne Coar

text: “Be on time.”
author: Norlynne Coar

text: “Cooley High was the movie that made me want to make films.”
author: George Tillman, Jr.

text: “Watching films is a very important tool because you can learn many aesthetics techniques.”
author: George Tillman, Jr.

text: “I have tried to get to know Spike Lee and guys that I have watched growing up, Francis Coppola and Martin Scorsese, and I try to learn as much as I can from them.”
author: George Tillman, Jr.

text: “I was a waitress for about eight months out of college, but that was it. From that point on, I have done Broadway, off-Broadway, stage, sop operas, commercials, movies, night-time series, voiceover work and animation.”
author: Vanessa Bell Calloway

text: “Do everything you think will work and the things that you think won’t - because sometimes, those are the things that really work for you.”
author: Vanessa Bell Calloway

text: “You have to go into your career not being afraid to fail.”
author: Brett Ratner

text: “Don’t let the industry’s perception of success or failure get to you.”
author: Ann Carli

text: “Always remember that if you’re in a position where you’re signing an artist or working with an artist, this is their whole life. It may be just a movie or a record to you. It may be just a six-week job to you, or two-year job to you, but this is their life.”
author: Ann Carli

text: “Understand that your commitment to a project is going to be for years, so make sure you really like the project.”
author: Ann Carli

text: “Don’t go by other people’s standards of how fast you should be moving up whatever ladder. This is a really hype-driven town.”
author: Ann Carli

text: “It’s important to see beyond the hype.”
author: Cassandra Mills

text: “Decide whether you want to be in this game for a career, or if you just want to make a quick dollar and get out. A career is longevity. A career is 10+ years and you still work.”
author: Cassandra Mills

text: “Understand the business.”
author: Cassandra Mills

text: “Read Billboard every week.”
author: Cassandra Mills

text: “…the industry is about money, and as an artist you become like a dollar. When you become an object like that, you have to know who you are personally.”
author: Kenny Lattimore

text: “There are so many artists who turn to drugs and alcohol, oversee, because they’re looking for reality once they get catapulted. For me, it is a strong sense of God that I turn to, not superficial things — because those things fade away.”
author: Kenny Lattimore

text: “A great song is not just a melody, it’s a mood.”
author: Seth Swirsky

text: “To be a successful songwriter, you have to hang out at studios. You have to hang out with artists, you gotta be at publishing companies….”
author: Seth Swirsky

text: “Come up with a winning idea and run with it. For example, if you discover a hot band or hot artist, the world will listen to you.”
author: Matthew Walden

text: “Be aggressive about your career. I’m always impressed with people who are aggressive. Even if the aggressiveness fails, people like me are impressed by it.”
author: Matthew Walden

text: “Weekends are spent listening to new music.”
author: Violet Brown

text: “Love what you do and really want it.”
author: Melissa Gilbert

text: “I knew I wanted to do this when I was 15 years old.”
author: Robi Reed

text: “I paid my dues until my big break as a casting director came along.”
author: Robi Reed

text: “ I always referred to myself as a Casting Director, even before I was.”
author: Robi Reed

text: “It’s great to be in places where everybody you meet has something to do with the business.”
author: John Mason

text: “Cannes is a great, great microcosm of the film business. It certainly includes all of the art and glamour, creativity, excitement and the stars.”
author: John Mason

text: “We tend to think that Hollywood or New York or Dallas or London is the center of the film business if we happen to live there, but I really isn’t. There’s a lot going on in a lot of places around the world.”
author: John Mason

text: “Sony hired me and it was just like car wash attendant one minute and board artist making $1,000 a week the next.”
author: Andres Alvarez

text: “I want unique content. I don’t want anyone else to sound like me or look lie me. When you see my film, I want you to say, ‘that’s him. That’s Andres.’”
author: Andres Alvarez

text: “I couldn’t think of a better time to be in animation than now.”
author: Andres Alvarez

text: “…if you want a career, consider that a lot of people started off as interns.”
author: Dr. Suzanne Regan

text: "The more you get involved, the more you understand where the industry’s going…”
author: Dr. Suzanne Regan

text: “Anybody can teach you how to push the buttons; but, they can’t give you the vision in your head. This is a God-given gift and this is how I express my creativity.”
author: TeeJ Mercer

text: “When friends of mine were having great summers, I was in L.A. interning and getting experience.”
author: TeeJ Mercer

text: “At the end of the day, I don’t know if we’ll turn out 100 or 50 films, but hopefully we’ll turn out 20 god ones that everybody remembers.”
author: Robert Teitel

text: “#1 is drive. You really have to love it. It’s one of these occupations and fields where if you don’t love it then it’s just not worth it."
author: Robert Teitel

text: “…you have to stick in there and ride it out.”
author: Robert Teitel

text: “To be a good producer I think you have to expect everything to go wrong. Perseverance.”
author: Robert Teitel

text: “The requirements for being a good singer are higher than many of those who waltz onto the set of American Idol think!”
author: Bobette Jamison-Harrison

text: “Vocal training will become, to a serious singer, a part of his or her lifestyle.”
author: Bobette Jamison-Harrison

text: “I’m the only vocal coach I know who will fire my students if I don’t see the progress that I know I should see within a certain period of time.”
author: Bobette Jamison-Harrison

text: “…you have to set the bar high for yourself.”
author: Jeff McMahon

text: “I like to play and I like to have my moment to shine, but when you’re playing with other people, it’s just like any other team — football, baseball, whatever — it’s important to step aside and let the other players do their parts”
author: Jeff McMahon

text: “i certainly love playing; but, I also have a role to play on stage as a performer. People come to see a show and we have to give them something they can share with us. We can’t just sit back in the shadows!”
author: Jeff McMahon

text: “Try to crew up on any shoots that you can — to gain knowledge.”
author: Andéa Clark

text: “Each video project might give you a chance to work with new technology or new production angles, shooting with green screens, copious amounts of water, or with hundreds of dancers. This means gaining experience in a variety of production situations,”
author: Andéa Clark

text: “The downside of this turnaround are the extremely long days, and a volatile work schedule - you never know where you’ll be working next.”
author: Andéa Clark

text: “You can’t try to write a hit. You just have to write a great song that will be a hit.”
author: Diane Warren

text: "I knew I wanted to do this the I was kid. When I was like seven years old I wanted to be a songwriter — before I even wrote a song.”
author: Diane Warren

text: “I was always, and am, quite a determined kind of person. Pretty driven. Ridiculously driven.”
author: Diane Warren

text: “I was hustling. I’d sit in a restaurant and if somebody was noted to me and I heard something about mis I was like ‘hi, what do you do? Can I give you a song?’
author: Diane Warren

text: “I was crazy. I threw songs into people’s cars. I’d follow them into the bathroom with a tape or cassette I wanted to be heard. I still want to be heard.”
author: Diane Warren

text: “Work hard and get great at it.”
author: Diane Warren

text: “In anything, it’s all about being great, attaining excellence and doing everything in your power to be the best at what you do — and then having the perseverance, dedication and serious drive to make that a reality.”
author: Diane Warren

text: “This is breathing to me.”
author: Diane Warren

text: “People will always want songs that touch them.”
author: Diane Warren

text: “If you listen to contemporary songwriting or what’s on the radio, you can’t - for the most part - go ‘wow, that’s an amazing song. I wish I wrote it.’ They’re not really songs as much; and, people still want songs.”
author: Diane Warren

text: “Save your money and be prepared to grind it out.”
author: Deidre Graham

text: “Be prepared to eat peanut butter and jelly sandwiches. Be prepared to sacrifice, to drink water instead of soda if you have to. If you persevere and really, really want to succeed, you’ll make it.”
author: Deidre Graham

text: “This was my path and I had no other choice really.”
author: Tina Davis

text: “I put God first and I know that He’s the only reason that I know a hit from a flop.”
author: Tina Davis

text: “On the performance side, I watched how artists performed and noticed what made the crowd react. That was important to me.”
author: The Late Gerald Levert

text: “My best advice is to talk to other working actors who make a living at their craft. Ask them what classes did they go to, then take acting classes to learn your craft and fine-tune your instrument.”
author: Chemin Bernard

text: “Know what category you fall in. It’s not about typecasting; it’s about knowing what you’re selling. Are you the leading man? A character actor? Know your accurate age range.”
author: Chemin Bernard

text: “Play to your strengths.”
author: Chemin Bernard

text: “You have to be willing to intern. And when you intern, you have to b a sponge.”
author: Chemin Bernard

text: “Come into the audition to plant a seed. Come in there to shine your light.”
author: Chemin Bernard

text: “Don’t give away your power.”
author: Chemin Bernard

text: “It’s either your job or it’s not. If it’s your job, there is nothing that you can do to lose it. You can do the worst reading in the world. On the other hand, if it’s not your job, there is nothing you can do to make us hire you.”
author: Chemin Bernard

text: “I see my name in the credits and I still go ‘yay!’ It still feels good to see your name up there.”
author: Karyn Usher

text: “…you have to get your foot in that door on the first job.”
author: Karyn Usher

text: “If you’re really passionate and really ready to work hard you’ll find that first job. After that, it’s just a mater of staying, working hard, moving around and meeting people…”
author: Karyn Usher

text: “Once you gain some experience as a staff writer, eventually you will climb the ranks. It’s essentially like being a freshman, sophomore, junior, senior. When you get to be a senior you get to be the producer.”
author: Karyn Usher

text: “Talk less and work more.”
author: Tess Taylor

text: “Surprise people with your brilliance or your brilliant project instead of just talking about it.”
author: Tess Taylor

text: “…having a plan makes a difference.”
author: Tess Taylor

text: “If you’re going to be an artist, signed to a label, you want to maximize every opportunity.”
author: Tina Campbell

text: "We absolutely love singing ad we absolutely love what we’re singing about.”
author: Erica Campbell

text: “Until we feel like it’s time to retire, there’s always new ways to grow, to improve, to reach new levels and dimensions.”
author: Tina Campbell

text: "In business you’re going to bump heads and disagree sometimes. But because we’re sisters, it’s generally over in a day.”
author: Erica Campbell

text: “We’ve gotten to a point where we respect what we bring to each other’s life professionally.”
author: Tina Campbell

text: “You have to build a team.”
author: Larry Shields

text: “…keep the faith; stay ambition; establish and build relationships. You can’t succeed without these three.”
author: Larry Shields

text: “Be as innovative as possible. If I see someone who obviously has an innovative approach, that’s different.”
author: Danielle Hinde

text: “1. Believe in God; 2. Believe in yourself; 3. Accomplish the goals you put forth. That’s how I’ve been living my life.”
author: Rodney “Darkchild” Jerkins

text: “People who know me or my legacy when I’m done will know that Rodney Jerkins had musical integrity and did real music.”
author: Rodney “Darkchild” Jerkins

text: “On the personal side, I’m real honest. People respect my honesty. I think I’m probably one of the most real dudes you’ll ever meet.”
author: Rodney “Darkchild” Jerkins

text: “I feel like I come from the cloth of Quincy Jones.”
author: Rodney “Darkchild” Jerkins

text: “I understand orchestration and I understand music for what it really is.”
author: Rodney “Darkchild” Jerkins

text: “…if there’s another person who has that potential like I had, I want him/her.”
author: Rodney “Darkchild” Jerkins

text: “I really challenge the artist and I tell it like it is.”
author: Rodney “Darkchild” Jerkins

text: “You should want someone to be real and give you constructive criticism, right?”
author: Rodney “Darkchild” Jerkins

text: “…know what you’re called to do and understand your purpose and calling in life — and go after it.”
author: Rodney “Darkchild” Jerkins

text: “There’s always something more that you can do. You can always win more races. You can always win more championships.”
author: Jeff Gordon

text: “Failure to me is never an option. I’m always trying to find a way to be successful.”
author: Jackie Joyner-Kersee

text: “I started running at the age of nine. I remember my first race. I finished last. That’s when I came up with the attitude that ‘ok, I need to improve a tenth of a second each time out, or jump 1/2 inch further.’””
author: Jackie Joyner-Kersee

text: “Each time I improved my time. I still might have been in 8th place but I knew I was getting better.”
author: Jackie Joyner-Kersee

text: “When I was 14, I saw the ’76 Olympic Games on television…and it all started to make sense.”
author: Jackie Joyner-Kersee

text: “For me, the Olympics will always be symbolic. It says a lot about being the best — willing to devote your time and energy for one opportunity. And you have to be ready on those given days.”
author: Jackie Joyner-Kersee

text: “To be in the company of so many great athletes who have made an Olympic team is truly and blessing, and it also applauds our hard work and commitment. Very few people can say that.”
author: Jackie Joyner-Kersee

text: “I think it’s important for our young people to have dreams and be aware of the commitments they make today so that tomorrow can be better.”
author: Jackie Joyner-Kersee

text: “Be true to who you really are.”
author: Jackie Joyner-Kersee

text: “Have a passion for whatever it is you want to do. And if it’s track and field, and you have that passion, you’ll find a way to do it."
author: Jackie Joyner-Kersee

text: “Close the deal!”
author: Dackeyia Q. Sterling

text: “Turn the lights off in the studio. Stop all the talking and get the deal on paper. Deal memos. Contracts. Copyrights. Agreements.”
author: Dackeyia Q. Sterling

text: “Greatness gets recognized.”
author: Dackeyia Q. Sterling

text: “Step up to YOUR future!”
author: Dackeyia Q. Sterling

text: "Get YOUR resume/YOUR career & YOURself red carpet and runway ready!”
author: Dackeyia Q. Sterling

text: “Working in the industry is a long journey, with mountains to climb, rivers to cross and races to run.”
author: Dackeyia Q. Sterling

text: “You can't just brown-nose your way to the top.”
author: Jennifer Davidson

text: “Impress your colleagues by taking work off their plates, too.”
author: Jennifer Davidson

text: “If you’re dong your job well, well notice that.”
author: Jennifer Davidson

text: “Every time you come into contact with bosses, as well as your coaigues, have a friendly, optimistic, helpful point of view.”
author: Jennifer Davidson

text: “Look around and see who you have connections to.”
author: Jennifer Davidson

text: #1 -  Always keep writing. Never give up. That’s the only thing you can control - you sitting in that chair and writing.”
author: May Chan

text: “Don't take it personal. Everybody gets notes. Everybody gets rewritten.”
author: May Chan

text: “I know a lot of artists say this, but I write because I have to.”
author: Kerri Grant

text: “Doing something repetitive soothes your mind, calms it, where you’re not focused on anything but that task. It also serves as a kind of cleanse for your mind.”
author: Kerri Grant

text: “Everybody says to write often, and that’s absolutely true. But, you can’t forget to read often.”
author: Jordan Harper

text: “Challenge yourself.”
author: Jordan Harper

text: “Make sure you have income to support yourself through the lean years.”
author: Kenneth Rance

text: “I’ve had six-figure years and I’ve had $6 years. I wrote my first screenplay while I was a phone operator at 1-800-DENTIST.”
author: Kenneth Rance

text: “There's an audience for everything.”
author: Kenneth Rance

text: “One of the biggest problems with the entertainment business is the pathos of fear.”
author: Hill Harper

text: “It's about doing something on a daily basis that moves your career and artistry forward…”
author: Hill Harper

text: “…move the ball forward.”
author: Hill Harper

text: “Getting to my dream has been a struggle, a joy and I would not change the journey for anything.”
author: Taraji P. Henson

text: “Get a good education. Study your craft. Be prepared.”
author: Taraji P. Henson

text: “Never give up.”
author: Taraji P. Henson

text: “I like being a storyteller, being passionate and true.”
author: Taraji P. Henson

text: “I enjoy the challenge of bringing new and wonderful characters to life.”
author: Taraji P. Henson

text: “My technique is all repetition. When I first get a script, I read it cover to cover so I get the idea of where everyone is coming from. Then, I read it from a different perspective and see myself in the role.”
author: Omar Gooding

text: “I’d love to do Martin Luther King, Joe Lewis, the real Tupac story, and anything where I can rub elbows with Denzel, my idol. That would be ideal.”
author: Omar Gooding

text: “It’s very important that people come off their electronics and do some thinking.”
author: Professor Vera J. Katz

text: “Spend some time reflecting.”
author: Professor Vera J. Katz

text: “Read the great writers and philosophers so that you get a perspective and a frame to life.”
author: Professor Vera J. Katz

text: “Pick the piece because something in it moves you and also tickles your memory bank.”
author: Professor Vera J. Katz

text: “Anyone can be emotional in front of a camera. To sustain it for more than one take is another story. To sustain it for seven performances a week in live theater cannot be done without a technique.”
author: Professor Vera J. Katz

text: “Learn as much as you can about the business side so you’re not making mistakes or going by what someone says.”
author: Synthia SAINT JAMES

text: “I research, research, research, research.”
author: Synthia SAINT JAMES

text: “The hardest thing for us as creative people is to figure out that fine line of marketing yourself and not sitting around waiting for someone to do it for you.”
author: Synthia SAINT JAMES

text: “When you see a Work for Hire contract, know that you’re giving up your copyright and you’re giving up all rights to that piece - so be cautious.”
author: Synthia SAINT JAMES

text: “Look at the fine print.”
author: Synthia SAINT JAMES

text: “Find a way to market yourself without being pushy.”
author: Synthia SAINT JAMES

text: “After I’ve finished painting, especially those days I get to paint all day, then I’ll get myself a glass of wine, turn on some music, go downstairs and dance. I celebrate it!”
author: Synthia SAINT JAMES

text: “Eventually your persistence will pay off.”
author: Janine Sherman Barrois

text: “Talent prevails and so does tenacity.”
author: Janine Sherman Barrois

text: “Remember, your career is a marathon, not a race.”
author: Janine Sherman Barrois

text: “Find your mentors and be a mentor.”
author: Melissa Houghton

text: “Find your supportive community.”
author: Melissa Houghton

text: “Go to festivals.”
author: Melissa Houghton

text: “See good work. It’s part of your job to watch tv and movies.”
author: Melissa Houghton

text: “Find out what really excites you and then find out who’s producing it, who’s supporting it.”
author: Melissa Houghton

text: “I never brag. I just try to get it done and keep it moving.”
author: Darrell D. Miller, Esq.

text: “Whatever you do, do it well.”
author: Darrell D. Miller, Esq.

text: “My biggest commodity is my time. It’s the thing that I most ferociously protect.”
author: Darrell D. Miller, Esq.

text: “Know how to deal with a lot of different personalities.”
author: Dana Arnett

text: "If you're fortunate enough to sit in the room where something new and exciting is going on, just watch and listen—because you pick it up and it’s very subtle.”
author: Dana Arnett

text: “Keep that positive energy that keeps creating more opportunities.”
author: Reginald Hudlin

text: "I lived two doors down from where Ike met Tina Turner and two doors down the other side from Brother Joe May, who was a famous gospel singer. So, I was equidistant between heaven and hell. That kind of cultural richness shaped a big part of who I am and the kind of stories I want to tell.”
author: Reginald Hudlin

text: “I’m obsessed with getting better and learning from others.”
author: Reginald Hudlin

text: “Better is better.”
author: Reginald Hudlin

text: “Keep sharpening your sword, developing your craft and raising the game of what you do.”
author: Reginald Hudlin

text: “I’m always looking for opportunities where I can work with the best and learn from them.”
author: Reginald Hudlin

text: “Keep writing whether the market likes it or not.”
author: The late Syd Field

text: “Many aspiring screenwriters do not really understand the concept of a screenplay, which is a story that is told with pictures.”
author: The late Syd Field

text: “…every screenplay you write is a positive experience, whether you sell it or get interest in it or not.”
author: The late Syd Field

text: “If you’re an audio engineer, you need to know who the president of Universal or Sony is —and know what their vision of what music is going to be years from now.”
author: Edward Petersen

text: “Once you get that first job, accept increasing responsibility because you will start becoming more and more valuable,”
author: Edward Petersen

text: “I love musicians who have dedicated their lives to their craft.…”
author: Edward Petersen

text: “Find a way to get some professional experience.”
author: Edward Petersen

text: “Develop very good job skills.”
author: Edward Petersen

text: “Gain industry knowledge.”
author: Edward Petersen

text: “My POWER ADVICE is never give up and work hard. That’s plain and simple.”
author: Rickie Weeks, Jr.

text: “You have to learn how to move on and try to get better at your craft -at any given moment.”
author: Rickie Weeks, Jr.

text: “One of the absolute best ways to get into the game industry is to work on an indie game.”
author: Kate Edwards

text: “Network like crazy and learn.”
author: Kate Edwards

text: “In the creative industries like games, movies and music, don’t tell me what you can do. Show me.”
author: Kate Edwards

text: “If the game’s a success and really shows off your skills, then that’s your resume right there.”
author: Kate Edwards

text: “There are so many great, wise people in the game industry who’ve been around for decades who are willing to talk to you about what they do and how they do it.”
author: Kate Edwards

text: “Get an education. There is nothing more valuable than knowledge.”
author: Rachael Stanley

text: “…you will be surprised how many areas of your job will draw on things you have learned from school.”
author: Rachael Stanley

text: “Learn to network.”
author: Rachael Stanley

text: “Reaching out to others in the entertainment industry is a vital tool in a successful career.”
author: Rachael Stanley

text: “Learn how to be a better interviewee and deal negotiator.”
author: Rachael Stanley

text: “It took me approximately one year to land my first celebrity client. That client was Mr. Idris Elba.”
author: Shawn Janifer

text: “Practice your craft. Network. Follow up.”
author: Shawn Janifer

text: “I remember the day that I decided I would only work with men, several people said it wasn’t possible. But, here I am with an all-male client roster.”
author: Shawn Janifer

text: “I love that my job has blessed me with the opportunity to travel the world.”
author: Shawn Janifer

text: “You have to produce creative work that is really superior!”
author: Robert McKee

text: “One of the big mistakes that beginning people make is they have just one idea.”
author: Robert McKee

text: “Find inspiration in the genre that you love.”
author: Robert McKee

text: “The secret to success in a career is excellence.”
author: Robert McKee

text: “You’ve got to find agents who are like you or represent people like you. Contact those agents and hook them.”
author: Robert McKee

text: “Realize that the first thing you ever write will be the worst thing you’ll ever write. It takes time”
author: Robert McKee

text: “We’re always dripping with creativity.”
author: Tirrell Whittley

text: “Motown Museum proudly supports Entertainment Power Players.”
author: Motown Museum

text: “CBS News salutes EPP for helping the world see itself as it is and as it can be.”
author: CBS News

text: “Writing is a muscle. We tend to think of it as inspiration - but it’s really perspiration.”
author: The Late Lynda Obst

text: "The more often yo write, the easier it is to write.”
author: The Late Lynda Obst

text: “Power is getting to make the things you want - and self-respect.”
author: The Late Lynda Obst

text: “The most important thing is to figure out how you’re going to get a good piece of material to control.”
author: The Late Lynda Obst

text: “Get control of a piece of material and get it made.”
author: The Late Lynda Obst

text: "My #1 tool is humor because it helps with charm, survival and frustration tolerance - and, it’s good in a meeting.”
author: The Late Lynda Obst

text: “Attrition, dropping out because of the inability to deal with rejection and frustration, kills more producers than flops an enemies.”
author: The Late Lynda Obst

text: “Give yourself a break.”
author: The Late Lynda Obst

text: “I've just been a huge, huge movie fan since I was 5 years old…”
author: Michael Hauge

text: “If you’re considering becoming a screenwriter, #1, you’ve got to watch lots of movies. And see the good movies twice so you can figure out how the principles of screenwriting are being applied.”
author: Michael Hauge

text: If you’re considering becoming a screenwriter, you MUST read scripts — two scripts a week until the end of time!”
author: Michael Hauge

text: “As a writer and storyteller, your goal must be to create and emotional experience for the reader of the script or the audience of the movie.”
author: Michael Hauge
